claims.text: Initially single-phase high-entropy alloys can develop brittle fracture because minor grain-boundary segregation reduces local cohesion.
Short-range ordering near grain boundaries can progressively reduce local cohesion.
Loss of grain-boundary cohesion can lead to intergranular crack initiation and propagation.
The proposed grain-boundary changes can lead to transgranular crack initiation and propagation.
Homogenized CoCrFeMnNi can have a single-phase solid-solution initial state.
The proposed initial material has uniform equiaxed grains, minimal second-phase precipitates, and suitability for demanding engineering service.
Trace-solute additions and controlled aging can induce grain-boundary compositional fluctuations or short-range order.
Testing from room temperature to 800 °C and at strain rates from 10^-4 to 10^-1 s^-1 is proposed to track the onset of embrittlement.
Solute-enriched grain-boundary environments can undermine grain-boundary cohesion.
Grain-boundary short-range ordered clusters can disrupt dislocation-mediated plastic flow.
Elevated-temperature segregation or nanoclustering of Cr, Ni, and Mn can promote grain-boundary decohesion in CoCrFeMnNi.
Cryogenic temperature promotes grain-boundary segregation or ordering that diminishes cohesion.
Accumulating segregation or ordering permits microcracks to initiate and propagate more readily, reducing toughness.
Prolonged segregation or ordering will shift fracture from ductile to partially brittle behavior and reduce fracture toughness.
Embrittlement will be accompanied by intergranular or cleavage-like fracture morphology.
A solution-treated high-entropy alloy with minimal segregation or ordering has relatively high toughness and ductile failure behavior.
Prolonged elevated-temperature aging can produce boundary changes associated with brittle failure.
Cryogenic exposure can promote segregation or ordering and cause a transition to quasi-brittle fracture.
Beyond a threshold amount of local grain-boundary change, brittle failure becomes predominant.
The hypothesis is falsified if embrittlement occurs without preceding or accompanying boundary segregation or ordering, or if increasing boundary fluctuations do not correlate with brittle fracture.
